resolution: The confirming instrument cleared my placementWorld suspect (no 'incl. placementWorld' in the line → it was not recomputing) and pointed at the real recurring cost: the session snapshot flush rewrote ALL 13 streams on every commit (~120ms — the PLACEFREEZE the user kept seeing), even though one commit touches one stream. That deferred flush freezes the UI ~260ms after each edit — the felt jank when placing rapidly. Fix: materializeSnapshots (cart/hmsc-int/data/index.ts) now skips any stream whose event count is unchanged since its last snapshot — the on-disk file stays valid because SNAPBOOT's count-vs-seq boot guard still agrees and the tail is empty, so a skip is correct; worst case if ever wrong is a slower boot via full replay, never lost work (DB events are the source of truth). materializedCount is seeded at boot from what each on-disk snapshot folded, so dirty-only kicks in from the first edit: 13 writes/commit → 1. Proven safe: a new data-store test asserts only the changed stream re-snapshots, an unchanged flush writes nothing, and a SKIPPED stream reopens with correct state (no data lost); 20/20 data tests pass. Cart-side, hot-reloads. Expect PLACEFREEZE to drop from streams=13 ms~120 to streams=1 ms~10, and gesture→rendered to fall accordingly. Sha 2d2910722. Remaining: pre ~130ms (the real piece-visible latency) is the next target if the user wants to push toward gameplay rate.
